alternatives: - **Runtime-fetch the canonical rows instead of vendoring** — rejected: the package's stated design is zero-network statics with a TanStack Query hook layered on top for live data; vendoring keeps the SSR/offline/no-cache fallback working exactly as today. - **Derive every literal-union tuple from the vendored JSON via a codegen step** (rather than hand-typing + pinning) — deferred: bigger surface change than this ticket's scope; the parity test gives the same safety guarantee today without touching the `as const` tuples' provenance.
consequences: - A backend canonical-row change that isn't followed by `pnpm sync-canonical` + a matching static update now fails this package's test suite immediately, instead of silently drifting until a bug report. - This package carries one more manual step (re-sync) whenever the backend changes a governed row; the failure mode if someone forgets is a loud test failure, not a silent one. - `src/canonical/reference-data.json` and the internal accessors in `src/canonical/index.ts` (other than `getCanonicalClassifications`) are not part of the package's public API — consumers should keep using the existing per-domain statics/formatters, not read the vendored JSON directly.
context: `@cellarnode/beverage-utils` ships hand-typed statics (`ACCESS_MODELS`, `PACKAGING_OPTIONS`, `CLOSURE_OPTIONS`, `ACTIVE_CURRENCIES`, `PROCUREMENT_CHANNELS`, `EnterpriseType`, `COUNTRY_CODES` + `STATIC_COUNTRY_LABEL_MAP`) that are each supposed to mirror one row of `cellarnode-backend-v2`'s canonical `reference_data` table. Before CEL-1604 nothing enforced that mirror: a backend row could change (a new packaging option, a renamed currency) and every frontend static would silently keep serving the stale list until a human noticed. This package also shipped zero test files, so even an accidental hand-edit of one of these tuples had no safety net. CEL-1604 (spec `docs/specs/2026-09-02-matching-canonical-deepening.md`, D13 + D27) pairs this with a backend change (PR #608) that commits a generated, deterministic dump of the canonical rows — `apps/cellarnode/src/db/canonical/reference-data.json` — behind a CI staleness check. The frontend half needs a way to consume that dump and prove its own statics are still correct against it.
decision: Vendor a verbatim copy of the backend's generated `reference-data.json` into this package at `src/canonical/reference-data.json`, refreshed by `pnpm sync-canonical` (`scripts/sync-canonical.mjs` — pure filesystem copy, never network or DB). Add a typed accessor module (`src/canonical/index.ts`) over that vendored JSON, and this package's first test suite (`__tests__/canonical-parity.test.ts`, vitest) which deep-equals every shipped static against the accessor for its corresponding row. Two derivation strategies, chosen per static: - Statics whose public type is a **hand-typed literal union** (`AccessModel`, `Packaging`, `Closure`, `Currency`, `ProcurementChannel`, `CountryCode`) stay hand-typed `as const` tuples — deriving them from the runtime JSON import would widen the type to plain `string` and change the public API. The parity suite pins them instead: any drift from the vendored row fails a test. - Statics whose public type is **not** a literal union (`STATIC_ACCESS_MODEL_REGISTRY`, `STATIC_PROCUREMENT_CHANNEL_REGISTRY`, the enterprise-type label map) are derived directly from the vendored JSON at module load, deleting the hand-typed duplicate. `getCanonicalClassifications()` is exported from the package root as the one new public accessor: `@cellarnode/ui`'s opportunity wizard hand-copies the category/subtype taxonomy today (`ui/src/opportunities/wizard/classification-options.ts`) because this package deliberately ships no classification static (the taxonomy is normally DB-driven at runtime). It should migrate to this accessor for its build-in fallback in a follow-up PR once it takes this package's release.
title: Vendor frontend reference statics from the backend's generated canonical JSON, pinned by a parity test
